title: token-recovery-hire-swap-and-price-anchoring-experiments
content:
Purpose:
A compact working sheet + playbook for (1) recovering token-unit economics after a sustained usage compression, (2) swapping temporary contractor/contract-hours into permanent hires with minimal runway impact, and (3) running lightweight price-anchoring experiments to re-calibrate PLG and enterprise price sensitivity. This doc is a hybrid: simple numeric scenarios + operational hiring swap SOP and experiment matrix.

Context and trigger: Q4 2025 saw a ~15% sustained drop in average tokens-per-customer-month vs baseline. Revenue stabilized but unit margin compressed due to fixed Dedicated capacity commitments. We need a response that preserves runway, reduces marginal cost, and tests price elasticity without damaging adoption.

Top-level assumptions (editable cells in attached sheet):
- Baseline ARR: $78.4M (month-of-reporting annualized)
- Monthly active token units: 200B tokens/mo (mix hosted:dedi:private = 60:30:10)
- Average cost-per-1k-tokens (current blended): $0.018
- Baseline gross margin: 62%
- Hiring cadence baseline: 6 net new FTE per quarter (prod/eng heavy)
- Contractor pool cost-per-FT-equivalent: 1.25x perm comp for 6mo engagements

Scenario design (3 knobs):
A) Headcount swap (temporary -> perm)
- Objective: convert 40% of contractor hours into perm roles over 3 quarters to save unit ops costs once ramped.
- Mechanism: freeze non-customer-facing perm roles for 2 quarters; prioritize perm offers for top-30% performing contractors; convert 0.6 contractor-FTE per critical product role.
- P&L effect (illustrative): perm hire fully loaded comp = $210k/year; contractor equivalent cost (annualized) = $265k/year. Swap saves ~$55k per FTE after hire, with 3–6mo ramp.

B) Burst-capacity hedging and demand-smoothing credits
- Objective: avoid purchasing extra reserved capacity while preserving enterprise SLAs.
- Mechanism: temporary token credits for customers hitting burst ceilings, combined with soft throttles and an A/B on a new 'burst-smoothing' premium add-on.
- Expected impact: shift 8% of peak-month usage into paid burst-smoothing add-on or deferred tokens within 30 days. Reduces immediate marginal GPU spend by ~6% in high-variance weeks.

C) Pricing anchor experiments (PLG + mid-market + enterprise cell tests)
- Objective: measure localized elasticity and find anchoring that recovers 3–6% of unit revenue without materially affecting adoption.
- Matrix (cells):
  * Test 1: PLG discount removal on heavy-token users (>1M tokens/mo) + small onboarding credit (one-time)
  * Test 2: Mid-market meter-tier reframe (rename + small bundle) at +5% list price but include latency SLA credit for top-tier
  * Test 3: Enterprise anchor: introduce a 'Commitment with burst' option priced at +8% vs current long-term slab but with guaranteed burst buffer and premium SRE support.
- Measurement windows: 6 weeks per cell, with matched cohorts and pre/post token behavior baseline. Primary KPIs: ARR uplift, churn within 90 days, new net retention, tokens-per-customer change.

Sensitivity matrix (high-level logic; see attached sheet for numbers):
- Dimensions: Price delta (-10% to +15%), Headcount swap speed (fast/med/slow), Burst adoption (0%/4%/8% of peak), Contractor-to-perm conversion rate (20%/40%/60%).
- Output metrics: change to monthly gross margin (bps), incremental ARR, runway delta (months).
- Key breakpoints identified: +5% price for mid-market recovers ~2.3% unit revenue at <0.5% churn; contractor swap at 40% yields ~180 bps margin improvement after 6 months.

Operational playbook: hiring swap SOP (quick checklist)
1) Inventory: run contractor performance snapshot; flag convertible roles with skills matrix (1 week).
2) Budget carve: allocate conversion budget from Q budget buffer (line item: contractor-conversion swap).
3) Offer cadence: batch offers in 4-week windows to control ramping and avoid comp inflation.
4) Onboarding: 30/60/90 ramp milestones tied to release cycle and cost-visibility (finance to monitor realized savings after 90 days).
5) Off-ramping: where conversion is not available, extend short-term contractor engagements only in mission-critical areas with explicit ROI targets.

Pricing experiment SOP (A/B test hygiene)
- Segment matching: use monthly token cohorts + product usage fingerprints; exclude >2% of strategic enterprise customers unless explicitly targeted.
- Metric cliffs: alert if churn >1.5x baseline or if activation rates drop >3ppt within first 14 days.
- Duration and power: aim for 95% power to detect 1.8% ARR uplift; typical run 6–8 weeks with 1:1 traffic split for PLG cells.
- Rollback guardrails: pre-defined rollback when leading indicators cross thresholds (churn, revenue per new sign-up, support-MTTI).

Example quick numbers (one-line summary of sheets):
- Fast Swap + Mid-market + Burst adoption = runway +1.9 months over 12 months, margin +220 bps at steady state (12mo).
- Slow Swap + No pricing + no burst = runway -0.6 months, margin -80 bps.
- Pricing-only aggressive (+10% across mid-market) = ARR +3.7% but churn risk concentrated in price-sensitive SME cohort (~4% increase).

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Comp inflation risk if conversions are publicized -> use private offers, stagger conversions.
- Customer backlash to price tests -> use clear comms for enterprise; for PLG rely on cohort isolation and onboarding credits.
- Measurement noise from seasonality -> use matched-window controls and bootstrapped confidence intervals.

What I need from partners (action items):
- Product: flag feasible product/latency credits and implement feature flags for pricing cells (owner: Priya)
- RevOps: prepare cohort lists and billing segmentation (owner: Eliot)
- Eng: support burst-smoothing add-on toggle and SLO credit mapping (owner: Samira)
- People Ops: provide contractor conversion comp bands and hiring ramp calendar (owner: Morgan/People Ops)
- Analytics: implement pre-specified queries and dashboards for weekly look (owner: Eliot Analytics)

Next steps (timeline):
- Week 0–2: finalize cells and sample sizes; lock sheet inputs, create QA runs (analytics + product)
- Week 3–8: run first wave of pricing + burst cells; batch 20 conversions for fast-swap sample
- Week 9–12: analyze, produce decision memo, and roll out approved changes to Q2 plan
